fig_05_cycle: Dollars peak in 2010, a year BEFORE deals do. Within named stages, green deal sizes fall 49.3pp more than non-green over 2007-12 [−69.3, −22.4]. The POOLED median falls alike in both: that comparison is confounded.
Green deal sizes fell far faster than non-green within the same stages
Green deals and disclosed green funding, all blocs, 2000–2012. Constant 2015 USD.

Source: Crunchbase 2013 Snapshot (CC BY 4.0); author's calculations. n = 2,174 green deals, of which 1,994 carry a disclosed amount. Counts and dollars are reported as separate series because undisclosed-amount rates differ systematically by instrument and bloc; panel (b) covers only the disclosed subsample. Constant 2015 USD via the US GDP deflator. The cheque-size claim is the WITHIN-STAGE comparison: the pooled median falls alike for green and non-green, but that is composition-confounded for both. Bootstrapped over 10,000 draws on clean stage codes, excluding the venture_unspecified catch-all: green −50.4% against non-green −1.1%, difference −49.3pp [−69.3, −22.4]. All 5 start- end pairs running to the window close are negative (−69.9 to −21.5pp), so the direction is robust to the start year; pairs stopping before the decline completes can turn positive, so it is sensitive to the end year. This is a size pattern, not an investor motive. Raw classifier output.

Source: Crunchbase 2013 Snapshot (CC BY 4.0); author's calculations. n = 41,105 deals, 2,174 green. The dollar series covers the disclosed subsample only, and both series are computed on that same subsample's denominator where dollars are concerned, so the comparison is internally consistent. A dollar share above the count share means the average green cheque exceeded the average cheque overall, which is consistent with green being capital-intensive; it does not test the cross-sector elasticity of Figure 1b. fig_09_power_wall: Every emerging-market test fails on the same wall, for different reasons
Observations available against the pre-registered minimum cell size, across H2–H5.
Observations available in the cell the test depends on

Source: Crunchbase 2013 Snapshot (CC BY 4.0); author's calculations. The minimum cell size of 30 was fixed in config before any hypothesis was tested, and no bar clears it. These are five distinct failures rather than one repeated: a difference-in-differences with no usable time series; an instrument-mix comparison resting on 3 non-dilutive deals, drawn from an emerging-market green sample of 34 which does itself clear the threshold; a graduation model with no entrants at all; a missing-middle transition holding 13 companies even in the best-covered bloc; and a need regressor on which 20 of 22 countries record exactly zero. Three figures that would have plotted these quantities as estimates were cut rather than drawn.

Source: Crunchbase 2013 Snapshot (CC BY 4.0); author's calculations. Deal counts before the analysis window is applied. Expressing each month as a share of its own year removes the level difference between years so the shapes are comparable.
